themes_detail.label: Park Rules Chaos & Noise Spike
themes_detail.summary: Park-related complaints exploded this week in St. George/Stapleton: 4 violations of park rules (vs. 0.2 weekly average) and 3 noise complaints from parks (vs. 0.1 weekly average), suggesting either new enforcement activity, organized gatherings, or emerging park safety/usability crisis.
evidence: Violation of Park Rules: 4 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (1500% spike, z-score 8.66)
Noise - Park: 3 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% spike, z-score 8.69)
Both spikes occurred simultaneously this week, suggesting concentrated event or pattern shift
reporting_angles: What triggered the sudden spike in park violations this week? Interview Parks Dept. and residents about what changed.
Are new organized gatherings or events creating noise disturbances? Check local event calendars and community boards.

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Surge
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints (Uber, Lyft, other rideshare) jumped to 7 this week from a baseline of 1.8 weekly complaints, a 300% spike, suggesting either increased illegal parking, traffic congestion, or safety incidents tied to rideshare activity.
evidence: For Hire Vehicle Complaint: 7 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.8 weekly average (300% spike, z-score 5.42)
This is a new emergence this week, not a multi-week trend
Aligns with broader city rideshare congestion issues but localized spike warrants investigation
reporting_angles: Interview residents in St. George about rideshare driver behavior (illegal parking, blocking driveways, traffic violations).
Check with TLC enforcement and local precincts: are there specific hotspots or repeated offenders?

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Blitz
themes_detail.summary: Street vendor enforcement complaints spiked dramatically 2 weeks ago (4 complaints vs. 0.1 baseline), a 3100% increase, suggesting either a city crackdown campaign or emerging vendor conflict in the district.
evidence: Vendor Enforcement: 4 complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.1 weekly average (3100% spike, z-score 11.72)
Spike occurred 2 weeks ago, not this week—less immediately urgent than other signals
Highest z-score (11.72) indicates statistically significant anomaly but with limited complaint volume
reporting_angles: Was there a city-wide or district-specific vendor enforcement campaign 2 weeks ago? Request records from Department of Consumer Affairs.
Interview street vendors in the district: are they being pushed out or facing new restrictions?

themes_detail.label: Tree Damage & Litter Infrastructure Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Last week saw a spike in dead/dying tree complaints (10 vs. 1.6 baseline, 515% increase) and illegal tree damage (4 vs. 1.2 baseline, 220% increase), coupled with litter basket requests up 191% this week, suggesting environmental neglect or recent storm damage requiring urgent Parks/Sanitation response.
evidence: Dead/Dying Tree: 10 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.6 weekly average (515% spike, z-score 5.31)
Illegal Tree Damage: 4 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly average (220% spike, z-score 4.16)
Litter Basket Request: 4 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.4 weekly average (191% spike, z-score 5.42)
Three-part environmental crisis unfolding over past 2 weeks
reporting_angles: Was there a recent storm or freeze damage that triggered tree complaints? Cross-reference weather data with complaint dates.
Interview Parks Dept. about tree maintenance backlog in CD 501—are they overwhelmed by requests?
Check if litter basket shortage is a chronic issue or new problem tied to park overcrowding.

themes_detail.label: Traffic Complaint Surge
themes_detail.summary: Traffic complaints jumped to 23 last week from a 5.2 weekly average, a 338% spike, indicating potential new congestion patterns, street design issues, or traffic enforcement problems that may be tied to the for-hire vehicle surge this week.
evidence: Traffic: 23 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 5.2 weekly average (338% spike, z-score 3.81)
Timing aligns with for-hire vehicle spike this week—possible causal connection
May reflect broader pattern of congestion rather than localized incident
reporting_angles: Map this week's traffic complaints: are they clustered around major streets/intersections or distributed?
Interview DOT and local precinct: are there known bottlenecks or new construction that could explain the surge?
